sections.title: The Major Judges
sections.description: The time of Othniel, Ehud, Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, and Samson

sections.title: Appendix
sections.description: Moral Decay in Israel: Micah's Idol and the War with Benjamin

events.title: Incomplete Conquest
events.description: After Joshua's death, the tribes continue to take possession of their territories, but none of them drive out all the Canaanites. Judah temporarily captures Jerusalem, but many tribes allow the Canaanites to live among them and make them forced laborers instead of driving them out.

events.title: The Angel of the Lord at Bochim
events.description: The angel of the Lord comes from Gilgal to Bochim and rebukes the Israelites for breaking the covenant by making alliances with the people of the land and failing to tear down their altars. The people weep loudly, and they name the place Bochim, which means 'weepers'.

events.title: The Pattern of Apostasy and Deliverance
events.description: After Joshua's death, Israel repeatedly turns away from the Lord and worships Baal and Ashtoreth. The Lord hands them over to their enemies, but when they cry out in distress, he raises up judges who rescue them. Yet the people continually return to idolatry.

events.title: The Nations Left Behind
events.description: The Lord leaves several nations in the land to test Israel and teach the new generations warfare. These peoples become a snare to the Israelites, who marry them and worship their gods.

events.title: Othniel - The First Judge
events.description: Israel sins, and the Lord hands them over to Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Aram-Naharaim, who oppresses them for eight years. The people cry out to the Lord, and he raises up Othniel, Caleb's nephew, to rescue them. The land has peace for forty years.

events.title: Ehud Kills King Eglon
events.description: Israel falls into sin again, and the Lord allows Moab's king Eglon to oppress them for eighteen years. Ehud, a left-handed Benjaminite, makes a double-edged sword and hides it under his clothes. He delivers tribute to Eglon and stabs the sword into the king's belly while they are alone. Then he leads Israel to victory over Moab.

events.title: Shamgar Defeats the Philistines
events.description: Shamgar, son of Anath, strikes down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad and saves Israel.

events.title: Deborah and Barak Defeat Sisera
events.description: The prophetess Deborah judges Israel under a palm tree in the hills of Ephraim. The Canaanite king Jabin oppresses Israel with his commander Sisera and nine hundred iron chariots. Deborah calls Barak to battle, but he refuses to go without her. They gather ten thousand men and defeat Sisera's army at the Kishon River. Jael kills Sisera with a tent peg.

events.title: Gideon Is Called
events.description: The Midianites oppress Israel for seven years and destroy their crops. The angel of the Lord appears to Gideon while he is threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites. The angel calls him to rescue Israel. Gideon tears down his father's altar to Baal and builds an altar to the Lord.

events.title: Gideon's 300 Men Defeat Midian
events.description: The Lord reduces Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300 men so that Israel cannot boast of its own strength. The three hundred men are equipped with trumpets, empty jars, and torches. During the night they surround the enemy camp, blow the trumpets, and smash the jars. The Midianites are seized with panic and turn their swords against each other.

events.title: Gideon's Ephod and Mistake
events.description: After the victory, Gideon pursues the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna and kills them. The people want to make Gideon their king, but he refuses. Instead, he makes an ephod from the gold plunder, which becomes a snare for him and his family. Israel worships the ephod as an idol. Gideon has seventy sons.

events.title: Abimelech's Tyranny
events.description: Abimelech, Gideon's son by a concubine from Shechem, kills his seventy brothers and makes himself king. Only the youngest, Jotham, escapes and tells a parable about trees seeking a king. After three years, God causes Abimelech and the citizens of Shechem to turn against each other. Abimelech dies when a woman drops a millstone on his head.

events.title: Tola and Jair
events.description: After Abimelech, God raises up Tola from Issachar, who judges Israel for twenty-three years. After him, Jair from Gilead judges for twenty-two years. He has thirty sons who ride on thirty donkey colts and control thirty towns.

events.title: Jephthah and His Vow
events.description: The Ammonites oppress Israel, and Jephthah, a skilled warrior who had been cast out by his brothers, is called back to lead the fight. Before the battle, Jephthah makes a rash vow to sacrifice whatever comes out of his house first to meet him. He defeats the Ammonites, but his only daughter comes out to greet him. She asks for two months in the mountains to mourn that she will never marry.

events.title: Ibzan, Elon and Abdon
events.description: After Jephthah, three lesser judges ruled Israel: Ibzan from Bethlehem for seven years, Elon from Zebulun for ten years, and Abdon from Ephraim for eight years.

events.title: The Birth of Samson
events.description: The Philistines oppressed Israel for forty years. The angel of the Lord appeared to Manoah's wife, who was childless, and promised her a son who would be a Nazirite from birth. The child was to begin delivering Israel from the Philistines. Samson was born, and the Spirit of the Lord began to stir him.

events.title: Samson and the Philistines
events.description: Samson wanted to marry a Philistine woman from Timnah. On the way there, he killed a lion with his bare hands. Later, he found honey in the carcass of the lion and posed a riddle at the wedding feast. When the Philistines solved the riddle by threatening his wife, he struck down thirty men in Ashkelon. He tied torches to three hundred foxes and burned the Philistine grain fields.

events.title: Samson and Delilah
events.description: The Philistine rulers bribe Delilah to discover the secret of Samson's strength. Three times Samson lies to her, but finally he reveals that his power lies in his hair, which has never been cut, because he is a Nazirite. Delilah gets a man to shave off his seven braids while he sleeps, and his strength leaves him. The Philistines capture him, gouge out his eyes, and set him to grind grain.

events.title: Samson's Death
events.description: The Philistines gather in the temple of Dagon to celebrate their victory over Samson. They bring him out to entertain them. Samson's hair has grown back again. He prays to the Lord for strength one last time, grabs the two central pillars of the temple, and brings it down upon himself and three thousand Philistines. He kills more in his death than during his life.

events.title: Micah's Idol
events.description: Micah from the hill country of Ephraim makes an idol and an ephod out of silver that his mother had dedicated to the Lord. He consecrates one of his sons as a priest, and later hires a Levite from Bethlehem. The Danites steal Micah's idol and the Levite on their way to capture Laish, and set up the idol in Dan.

events.title: The Levite's Concubine
events.description: A Levite from the hill country of Ephraim travels with his concubine through Gibeah in Benjamin. The men of the city surround the house where they are staying and demand to abuse the Levite. Instead, he sends out his concubine to them, and they mistreat her all night until she dies. The Levite cuts her body into twelve pieces and sends them to all the tribes of Israel as a witness to the wickedness.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: The War Against Benjamin
events.description: All Israel gathers against Benjamin to punish the wickedness at Gibeah. The Benjamites refuse to hand over the guilty men. In two battles, Israel is defeated, but on the third day the Lord gives them victory. Almost the entire tribe of Benjamin is wiped out. The six hundred surviving men lack wives, and Israel finds a solution by giving them women from Jabesh Gilead and from Shiloh. The book ends with these words: 'In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.'
